joint_recovery.position_reference_note: Same rule as P0 (the controller's own position target), extended to RAPTOR: its internal target is not published on trajectory_setpoint, so while RAPTOR owns the actuators the target is its logged capture (activation reset or setpoint-stale hold); classic stages use trajectory_setpoint as in P0. trajectory_setpoint-only and fixed NED results are kept as comparisons.

p1.speed_rationale: Requested starting values kept. Travel along +N is accel_s*v/2 + cruise_s*v (S3: 5.0 m, S2: 2.5 m) plus braking; the worst case stays below 7 m, leaving at least 3 m to the frozen 10 m safety radius, and 0.5 m/s^2 ramp acceleration is gentle for both controllers.
p1.reference: Before the subject event the outgoing controller tracks one runner-published trajectory_setpoint (position ramp, velocity and acceleration feed-forward, constant yaw) starting from its own current target: classic through OFFBOARD, RAPTOR through its external trajectory_setpoint input. At the event the stream stops and the incoming controller uses its original mechanism: RAPTOR mode-entry reset holds the activation position/yaw with zero velocity; classic AUTO_LOITER brakes to the navigator loiter point.
p1.baselines: p1_baseline_classic: classic OFFBOARD motion then AUTO_LOITER (same takeover mechanism, no controller switch). p1_baseline_raptor: RAPTOR external-setpoint motion then the stream stops; after RAPTOR's 200 ms setpoint timeout it holds its position (same capture rule as mode entry, no reset or switch).

motor_saturation.note: actuator_motors control in [0,1]; upper/lower limit within 1e-3
